records.title: Normative language and stable requirement identifiers
records.disposition: Only exact uppercase MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY terms carry normative force. Every new or materially changed normative clause cites a monotonic YWE-REQ-NNNN identifier, and allocated identifiers are never renumbered, reused, or deleted.
records.context: The repository needs one explicit vocabulary for binding clauses and permanent identifiers that remain stable across revisions.
records.decision: Only exact uppercase MUST, MUST NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, and MAY terms carry normative force. Every new or materially changed normative clause cites a monotonic YWE-REQ-NNNN identifier, and allocated identifiers are never renumbered, reused, or deleted.
records.rationale: Explicit force and permanent identifiers make conformance claims testable and preserve traceability when prose moves or is superseded.
consequences: Lowercase keyword uses remain descriptive rather than implicitly binding.
Terminal requirement records remain in the register and material semantic changes allocate new identifiers.

records.title: Typed governance records and durable rationale
records.disposition: Material governance work is recorded in typed ADR, CP, RISK, DEV, or Q records. Every material decision retains durable rationale, and each glossary concept has one canonical definition.
records.context: Material decisions, proposals, risks, deviations, and questions previously lived across prose and historical logs without one typed lifecycle authority.
records.decision: Material governance work is recorded in typed ADR, CP, RISK, DEV, or Q records. Every material decision retains durable rationale, and each glossary concept has one canonical definition.
records.rationale: Typed records preserve history, make lifecycle state reviewable, and prevent transient discussion from becoming hidden authority.
consequences: The machine register is the current record authority while historical logs remain provenance.
Semantic questions close only through a linked accepted decision, and duplicate concept definitions are governance defects.

records.title: Immutable ontology and mutable truth-scoped worldstate
records.disposition: The nine-coordinate base ontology is immutable. Mutable consequences are separate truth-scoped, typed, provenance-bearing state deltas. Perception may vary an observer's view but cannot rewrite shared truth.
records.context: Static-world wording conflicted with lawful worldstate and location mutation contracts and left perception boundaries implicit.
records.decision: The nine-coordinate base ontology is immutable. Mutable consequences are separate truth-scoped, typed, provenance-bearing state deltas. Perception may vary an observer's view but cannot rewrite shared truth.
records.rationale: Separating structural ontology from scoped state preserves cosmological invariants while allowing auditable consequences and observer-specific knowledge.
consequences: Ontology changes are not represented as ordinary worldstate deltas.
State mutation and perception outputs require explicit truth scope and provenance.

records.title: Realm and coordinate vocabulary
records.disposition: Realm and plane remain equivalent labels for one ontology category. Coordinate index and bit position identify a structural slot; ordinal identifies sequence rank; presentation order controls display only; realm or plane identity names the ontology member; and a full vector or state identity is the complete value. None is inferred from another without an explicit mapping.
records.context: Realm, plane, coordinate, bit position, ordinal, presentation order, and full state identity were used without one explicit distinction.
records.decision: Realm and plane remain equivalent labels for one ontology category. Coordinate index and bit position identify a structural slot; ordinal identifies sequence rank; presentation order controls display only; realm or plane identity names the ontology member; and a full vector or state identity is the complete value. None is inferred from another without an explicit mapping.
records.rationale: The distinction prevents a display convention or sequence rank from silently changing structural or state identity.
consequences: Mappings between presentation, ordinal, coordinate, and identity representations must be explicit.
Realm and plane remain aliases for the same ontology category rather than separate structures.

records.title: Symbolic grammar ownership and ASH dependency identity
records.disposition: The ASH Cosmological Model owns upstream symbolic grammar. The ASH dependency is pinned by the deterministic content digest recorded in data/governance/ash_dependency_identity.json; a path, branch name, or mutable label alone is not a dependency identity.
records.context: The repository identified ASH as upstream authority but did not bind symbolic-grammar ownership to one content-addressed dependency identity.
records.decision: The ASH Cosmological Model owns upstream symbolic grammar. The ASH dependency is pinned by the deterministic content digest recorded in data/governance/ash_dependency_identity.json; a path, branch name, or mutable label alone is not a dependency identity.
records.rationale: A named owner resolves semantic authority while a content digest makes the exact dependency state reproducible and reviewable.
consequences: YWE interpretation may consume ASH symbolic output but cannot redefine the upstream grammar.
Any accepted ASH dependency change updates the pinned digest and receives durable governance review.

records.title: Wolf resonance canonical term and migration alias
records.disposition: wolf_resonance is the canonical read/write field. wolf_alignment is accepted only as a compatibility read or migration alias and is never emitted as new canonical state. The dual-variable model describes distinct resonance pressures and is non-moral.
records.context: Historical wolf_alignment fields coexist with preferred wolf_resonance wording and can be misread as a moral scale.
records.decision: wolf_resonance is the canonical read/write field. wolf_alignment is accepted only as a compatibility read or migration alias and is never emitted as new canonical state. The dual-variable model describes distinct resonance pressures and is non-moral.
records.rationale: A one-way alias preserves legacy readability without maintaining two competing write authorities or changing Twin Wolf canon.
consequences: New normative schemas and examples use wolf_resonance.
Legacy wolf_alignment input is normalized without treating either variable as good or evil.

records.title: Append-only history and compensating reversal
records.disposition: Accepted events remain append-only. A reversal or correction is a new provenance-bearing compensating delta that changes current state; it never deletes or rewrites the accepted event that produced the earlier effect.
records.context: Append-only history requirements coexist with lawful correction and reversal of current-state effects.
records.decision: Accepted events remain append-only. A reversal or correction is a new provenance-bearing compensating delta that changes current state; it never deletes or rewrites the accepted event that produced the earlier effect.
records.rationale: Separating historical fact from current effect preserves auditability while allowing lawful recovery, correction, and reversal.
consequences: Histories retain both the original event and its compensating delta.
Current state is derived by applying accepted deltas in deterministic order.

records.title: Truth authority lattice
records.disposition: Truth authority is monotonic: a lower-authority layer may specialize only within freedoms left by higher constraints and cannot overwrite them. Conflicts are rejected or contained rather than resolved in favor of the lower layer.
records.context: Multiple truth scopes and authored overlays require a formal rule for conflicts between authority layers.
records.decision: Truth authority is monotonic: a lower-authority layer may specialize only within freedoms left by higher constraints and cannot overwrite them. Conflicts are rejected or contained rather than resolved in favor of the lower layer.
records.rationale: Monotonic authority prevents local, player, perception, or authored overlays from silently rewriting shared structural truth.
consequences: Resolvers compare proposed changes against all higher applicable constraints.
A blocked lower-layer change produces an explicit rejection or diagnostic rather than a hidden overwrite.

records.title: Normative YWE Core and WRW reference-profile separation
records.disposition: YWE Core contains platform-neutral reusable normative contracts. Where Ravens Wait content remains a reference profile, fixture, or game-layer specialization and cannot create universal YWE Core rules merely by exercising a core contract.
records.context: WRW reference material appears beside reusable YWE contracts and can be mistaken for universal engine truth.
records.decision: YWE Core contains platform-neutral reusable normative contracts. Where Ravens Wait content remains a reference profile, fixture, or game-layer specialization and cannot create universal YWE Core rules merely by exercising a core contract.
records.rationale: Explicit scope preserves reuse and prevents one reference game from silently constraining every conforming YWE world.
consequences: Every material artifact receives an unambiguous scope classification.
WRW fixtures may prove a generic contract but do not promote WRW-specific canon into YWE Core.

records.title: Authoritative ASH source and generated specification mirror
records.disposition: core/ash_pattern_engine/canonical is the authoritative source. specs is a deterministic generated mirror maintained by scripts/sync_ash_specifications.py and bound to the digest in data/governance/ash_dependency_identity.json. Direct independent edits to the mirror are not authoritative.
records.context: core/ash_pattern_engine/canonical and specs contain parallel ASH specification trees without a single declared source/mirror direction.
records.decision: core/ash_pattern_engine/canonical is the authoritative source. specs is a deterministic generated mirror maintained by scripts/sync_ash_specifications.py and bound to the digest in data/governance/ash_dependency_identity.json. records.rationale: A one-way source/mirror relationship eliminates split authority while retaining the existing consumer-facing specs path.
consequences: ASH changes begin in the canonical source and regenerate the mirror deterministically.
Synchronization validation blocks drift, untracked mirror-only content, and digest mismatch.
